issues.legal_issue: Time for depositing rent arrears should not be extended where the tenant’s conduct does not justify the exercise of discretion.
material_facts: The tenant had defaulted in paying rent for several years.
The tenant relied on an adjustment of rent that the lower courts found false and supported by a document they found inauthentic.

Although the tenant disputed the contractual rent and asserted that a lower rent was payable, the tenant waited more than two years after receiving the eviction notice to apply for fixation of the standard rent.
After the standard rent was fixed, the tenant still did not deposit the rent due before the trial or appellate proceedings concluded.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming the appellate court had power to extend the time for depositing the arrears, the facts did not justify exercising that discretion in the tenant’s favour. The Court did not decide whether the statutory reference to the relevant court included an appellate court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court did not determine the scope of Section 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947. It held only that, on these facts, extending the time for payment would not have been justified.

rule.if: appeal_from_rent_control_eviction_decision and (persistent_rent_default and false_rent_adjustment_claim and delayed_standard_rent_application and rent_unpaid_after_standard_rent_fixed)

predicates.appeal_from_rent_control_eviction_decisi: The tenant appealed from a decision in an eviction proceeding governed by rent-control law.
predicates.persistent_rent_default: The tenant repeatedly failed to pay rent over a prolonged period.
predicates.false_rent_adjustment_claim: The tenant claimed rent had been discharged by an adjustment that the courts found false and supported by inauthentic evidence.
predicates.delayed_standard_rent_application: The tenant waited a substantial period after disputing the rent to apply for its fixation.
predicates.rent_unpaid_after_standard_rent_fixed: The tenant did not pay the rent due even after the standard rent had been fixed.

issues.definition: When a tenant appealing an eviction decision has persistently defaulted, advanced a false adjustment claim, delayed seeking fixation of the rent, and remained unpaid after that fixation, time for payment is not extended.

issues.legal_issue: The challenged eviction notice was valid.
material_facts: The landlord issued an eviction notice under Section 12(2) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947.
The tenant challenged the notice’s validity.
The trial and appellate courts considered the challenge, and the Supreme Court agreed with their conclusions.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the challenge and upheld the validity of the eviction notice.
issues.legal_principle: The Court agreed with the trial and appellate courts’ conclusions on the notice under Section 12(2) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, without setting out a separate general test or further reasoning.

predicates.appeal_from_rent_control_eviction_decisi: The tenant appealed from a decision in an eviction proceeding governed by rent-control law.
predicates.eviction_notice_challenged: The tenant disputed the validity of the landlord’s eviction notice.
predicates.lower_courts_found_notice_valid: The trial and appellate courts considered the notice challenge and concluded that the notice was valid.

issues.definition: If a tenant challenges an eviction notice in an appeal and the lower courts have found it valid, the notice is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee landlord may obtain an eviction decree when the suit was validly instituted by the transferor landlord and the transfer occurs during the suit.
material_facts: When the eviction suit was instituted, the original landlord owned the premises and had a valid cause of action based on the tenant’s rent default.
The original landlord transferred the premises to the transferee landlord while the suit was pending, and the transferee was added as a plaintiff.
The Court proceeded on the basis that the transfer included the original landlord’s rights in the premises and in any decree that might be passed.
The tenant had not paid or tendered the arrears to obtain the statutory concession against eviction.
issues.conclusion: The assignment did not prevent a decree for possession in favour of the transferee landlord, and the tenant’s contention that no such decree could be passed was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: A suit that was validly instituted on an existing cause of action ordinarily proceeds to decree unless the law requires otherwise; a later event must necessitate denial of the relief to defeat it. Under Section 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, paying or tendering the arrears is a concession a tenant may use to avoid eviction. The Court distinguished Sm. Daya Debi v. Chapala Debi because the assignment there preceded institution of the suit, and noted that it need not rely on Kanto M. Mullick v. Jyotisk Chandra Mukherjee.

rule.if: appeal_from_eviction_decree and cause_of_action_existed_at_filing and assignment_during_suit and transferee_received_landlord_rights and tenant_did_not_pay_or_tender_arrears

predicates.appeal_from_eviction_decree: A party appealed from a decree in an eviction suit.
predicates.cause_of_action_existed_at_filing: The landlord had a valid basis for seeking eviction when the suit was instituted.
predicates.assignment_during_suit: The landlord transferred the premises to another person while the eviction suit was pending.
predicates.transferee_received_landlord_rights: The transfer included the transferor’s rights in the premises and in any decree that might be passed in the suit.
predicates.tenant_did_not_pay_or_tender_arrears: The tenant did not pay or tender the arrears to obtain the statutory protection against eviction.

issues.definition: When an eviction suit was validly instituted, the landlord transfers the property and associated rights during the suit, and the tenant does not pay or tender the arrears, the transferee landlord may obtain a possession decree.
